items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me, Buddy DeFranco, and a saxophone player.

ctx.x: . . . a bigger part of the fee.

They wanted to get Basie out of debt, so they put a small band around him, paid him a small salary. As a matter of fact, Buddy DeFranco, the clarinet player – caucasian cat. You know who he is – he was making more money than Basie was, and they put him in Basie’s band. The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. items.title: 68154_Gus Johnson oral history interview
items.q: It was me, Clark Terry, Jimmy Lewis, Buddy DeFranco, Bob Garth.

ctx.x: Oh, yes, Freddie was out of the band. I said, 'Where's Freddie Green?' He said, 'Well, I got this job in Chicago and I booked just for a small band, six pieces.' I said, 'Man, you better get Freddie Green back in this band,' just like that. And we made the job in Chicago, at the Brass Rail. And Freddie wasn't with us. It was me, Clark Terry, Jimmy Lewis, Buddy DeFranco, Bob Garth.] He's a tenor player.
